references.text: Joseph's first dream, in which his brothers' sheaves bow down to his sheaf, hints at the respect and submission they later show him, fulfilled in this scene.
Joseph's second dream, where the sun, moon, and eleven stars bow to him, further points to his brothers' submission to Joseph in Egypt.
Joseph's brothers bow before him during their first meeting in Egypt, beginning the fulfillment of Joseph's dreams.
Joseph's brothers bow again before him under dramatic circumstances when Benjamin is accused, further emphasizing their submission.
After Jacob's death, Joseph's brothers fall down before him and ask for forgiveness, showing the continued fulfillment of the dreams.
A powerful theological contrast showing the brothers' journey from hostility (37:23) to full submission (43:26), highlighting God's plan of reconciliation.
A typological parallel where submission to Joseph in the Old Testament mirrors the worship of Jesus in the New Testament.
The verses describe the same sequence of events from two perspectives: the journey with the gift (43:15) and the arrival with submission (43:26).
